title: 256 bit RAM

sources.document: National Semiconductor 1977 Memory Databook, DM54S200/DM74S200 256-bit read/write Schottky memories with TRI-STATE outputs
sources.familyUsed: DM74S200 (Schottky); no datasheet for a plain 74200 was found

pins.name: ME1'
pins.text: memory enable; all three must be low

pins.name: WE'
pins.text: write enable, active low; while low the output is in high impedance

pins.name: Y
pins.text: output: the stored bit, which is the complement of the data written

functions.formula: Y = MEM[address] when ME1'=ME2'=ME3'=L AND WE'=H; otherwise Z
functions.text: Read: the stored bit (complement of the data that was written) appears at Y. Any ME' high, or WE' low (write), puts Y in high impedance.

state.changesOn: WE' low while ME1', ME2', ME3' are all low (level-sensitive write)
rules: Write: ME' all low and WE' low: MEM[address] = NOT DATA (the complement is stored); output Z
Read: ME' all low and WE' high: Y = MEM[address]
Inhibit: any ME' high: Y = Z, no write
Address: row decoder A,B,C,H (pins 1,2,15,14) and column decoder D,E,F,G (pins 7,9,10,11), 16 x 16 matrix

electrical.notes: DM74S200: VCC 4.75-5.25 V, TA 0-70 C, IOH -5.2 mA, IOL 16 mA, VOL max 0.45 V. PNP inputs: IIL max -250 uA (one-eighth of a 74S load). Off-state output current 50 / -50 uA.
